source.author: verg
source.text: Non me impia namque Tartara habent, tristes umbrae, sed amoena piorum concilia Elysiumque colo.
source.text_original: Non me impia namque / Tartara habent, tristes umbrae, sed amoena piorum / concilia Elysiumque colo.
source.text_english: For impious Tartarus does not hold me, nor the sad shades, but I dwell in the pleasant company of the righteous and in Elysium.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: miseris tu gentibus, Argo, fata paras, nec iam merito tibi, Tiphy, quietum ulla parens volet Elysium manesque piorum.
reuse.text_original: miseris tu gentibus, Argo, / fata paras, nec iam merito tibi, Tiphy, quietum / ulla parens volet Elysium manesque piorum.
reuse.text_english: For wretched peoples, Argo, you prepare fates, nor will any parent now rightly wish tranquil Elysium for you, Tiphys, or the shades of the righteous.
